A hand-knotted Persian or a Kashmiri silk piece needs to be dusted dry, washed flat, rinsed until the water runs clear, then dried in controlled conditions before the pile is groomed back. None of that happens on a balcony or in a bathroom, and a rented steam machine run over wool by house help usually makes things worse — the pile mats, the dyes move, and the smell that follows a damp wool rug through a closed, air-conditioned flat is worse than the stain that started it.

So we collect. Wash4You picks up from your door, free, and the rug is cleaned off site where it can be handled flat and dried fully.

**What we actually see here.** Dining-room rugs with a slow ring of spills near one chair. Silk with a shine gone flat where a sofa leg sat. Fringes greyed while the field is still clean. Pale wool in a west-facing living room that has quietly turned the colour of the air outside. Machine-made polypropylene runners in the entrance foyer that take everything the lift lobby brings in. Each of these is a different job — silk and wool are not treated the same way, and we say so before we take the rug, not after.

Tell us the tower and we coordinate with your concierge or gate desk directly, so nobody needs to be chased. faqs.a: Usually, yes — that smell is moisture and soil trapped deep in the pile and backing, which surface vacuuming never reaches. It needs a full wash and, more importantly, a properly controlled dry. That is exactly why the rug has to leave the flat.
